text: Cities across India are experimenting with electric buses to cut air pollution and fuel costs. Transport agencies say an electric bus costs more to buy than a diesel one, but is far cheaper to run because electricity costs less per kilometre and there are fewer moving parts to maintain. Several cities now lease buses from private operators and pay per kilometre, which lowers the upfront burden on public budgets. Charging remains the main challenge. Depots need strong grid connections, and many older depots were not designed with space for chargers. Planners are working with power utilities to upgrade connections and to schedule charging at night, when electricity demand is low.
reference: Indian cities are trialling electric buses that cost more upfront but less to run, often through per-kilometre leasing. Charging infrastructure at depots is the main obstacle, so planners are upgrading grid connections and charging at night.

text: Public libraries are changing to meet new demands. Many now lend tools, seeds and musical instruments alongside books, and offer free workshops on topics such as résumé writing and basic coding. Librarians report that visitor numbers have risen at branches that added community programs. Funding, however, has not kept pace, and several branches have reduced opening hours. Supporters argue that libraries provide a free, safe space that serves people of every age and income, and they want stable long-term funding.
reference: Libraries now lend items beyond books and run community workshops, which has raised visits, but funding has lagged and some branches have cut hours. Supporters want stable funding for these free public spaces.
